title.en: Avoir helps tell a completed event

summary.en: Hear the helper verb and the past participle together.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 2.

Episode 2 includes *Il a avalé une guêpe* and *J'ai perdu un ami très cher*. In these lines a present form of *avoir* combines with a past participle to tell a past event.

Notice the two parts: *a + avalé*, *ai + perdu*. A participle does not always end in `-é`: *perdu* belongs to a different pattern. It is useful to learn a verb's participle along with its infinitive.

Not every French past event uses *avoir* as its helper. Some use *être*, as in another line in the same scene. Start by recognising the complete verb group rather than treating every short *a* as an independent statement about possession.

For listening practice, identify who the subject is, then listen for the short helper before the longer action word. That small helper can be easy to miss in connected speech.
